newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich supports concept of outside board for IRS.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich supports concept of outside board for IRS.

text.p: U.S. House Speaker Newt Gingrich said he supported the concept of an independent board to oversee the IRS, a key recommendation from a review released Wednesday.

"We'll do everything we can on the House side to move this," Gingrich said at a new conference called to unveil the report. In response to questions, he said "I absolutely support the concept' of an independent board to oversee the Internal Revenue Service.

House Majority Leader Dick Armey, Texas Republican, said he might support an independent board but he described the step as "an incidental point to everyone except the Treasury" compared to the goal of tax simplification.

Five of the 16 members of the National Commission on Restructuring the Internal Revenue Service dissented from the recommendation for a seven-member board, drawn mostly from the private sector, to manage the IRS. The agency would remain as part of the Treasury Department.
The Clinton administration strongly opposed the proposal as potentially unconstitutional and needless tinkering that might disrupt tax collection.

Included in the report were 52 recommendations for tax simplification, including abolition of the alternative minimum tax, encouraging electronic filing and spreading out the deadline, now April 15, for filing person income taxes.

The presidentially appointed board proposed by the commission would have five members from "large service organizations." Its other members would be the secretary of the Treasury and a representative from the labor union representing IRS workers.
Under the plan, Treasury would retain full control of tax policy. The commissioner of IRS would be appointed to a five-year term.
